sentences.en: In the first century BC, the philosopher Athenodorus was looking for a house to rent in Athens.
sentences.zh: 公元前一世纪，哲学家雅诺多罗斯在雅典寻找出租的房屋。

sentences.en: He found one at a remarkably good rate, given how large it was, and he soon realised why.
sentences.zh: 鉴于房子那么大，他以极优惠的价格租到了一处，但很快他就明白了原因。

sentences.en: On the very first night he was working late, when a ghost appeared with a long beard and bristling hair, clanking its iron fetters.
sentences.zh: 就在第一天深夜他还在工作时，一个拖着沉重铁镣、留着长须和硬毛的鬼魂出现了。

sentences.en: The ghost led him outside and indicated a spot in the courtyard.
sentences.zh: 鬼魂将他领到外面，指了指庭院里的一个地方。

sentences.en: And the next day, when Athenodorus had the spot dug up, his men found a pile of old bones.
sentences.zh: 第二天，当雅诺多罗斯让人在那个地方开挖时，他的手下发现了一堆旧骨头。

sentences.en: And after the bones had been laid to rest, the house was haunted no more.
sentences.zh: 骨头入土为安后，这栋房子就再也没有闹过鬼了。

sentences.en: Tom Holland, that is a great story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰，这真是一个极好的故事，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a fabulous...
sentences.zh: 这太美妙了……

sentences.en: It's from Pliny.
sentences.zh: 这是出自老普林尼。

sentences.en: Isn't it from Pliny?
sentences.zh: 难道不是出自老普林尼吗？

sentences.en: It is, the younger Pliny.
sentences.zh: 是的，是小普林尼。

sentences.en: But I remember it from childhood.
sentences.zh: 但我对它的记忆始于童年。

sentences.en: I had the bumper book of ghosts, and that was the very first story in it.
sentences.zh: 我曾有一本厚厚的幽灵故事书，而那正是书中的第一个故事。

sentences.en: And it had a fabulous black and white illustration of Athenodorus and the ghost with the manacles and the beard creeping up behind him.
sentences.zh: 里面有一幅极棒的黑白插图，画的是雅诺多罗斯，还有那个戴着手铐、留着胡子、正悄悄从他身后逼近的鬼魂。

sentences.en: So I remember it very, very vividly.
sentences.zh: 所以我对它记忆犹新。

sentences.en: And the ghosts have always...
sentences.zh: 而且那些幽灵一直……

sentences.en: I've always loved stories about ghosts.
sentences.zh: 我一直很喜欢关于鬼魂的故事。

sentences.en: And in fact, over the course of the lockdown, one of my activities was to go on ghost hunting walks across London.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在封锁期间，我的活动之一就是进行贯穿伦敦的寻鬼徒步之旅。

sentences.en: So I did two huge walks up to the tower, across London, back down again.
sentences.zh: 所以我进行了两次漫长的徒步，走到伦敦塔，穿过伦敦，然后再走回来。

sentences.en: And I went right the way up to Highgate Cemetery, which boasts perhaps the most haunted road in Britain.
sentences.zh: 我一直走到了海格特公墓，那里拥有据称是英国闹鬼最凶的路段。

sentences.en: It's got the Highgate vampire.
sentences.zh: 那里有海格特吸血鬼。

sentences.en: It's got a kind of strange psychic blob that creeps up on people and then leaps away.
sentences.zh: 那里有一种奇怪的灵异光团，会悄悄靠近人们然后又跳开。

sentences.en: All kinds of terrifying things.
sentences.zh: 各种各样吓人的东西。

sentences.en: But at the top of that road, there is Pond Square, which boasts perhaps my favourite ghost of all time.
sentences.zh: 但在这条路的尽头，是庞德广场，那里有着我个人最喜欢的历代鬼魂。

sentences.en: Pond Square is where Francis Bacon, in 1626, attempted to deep freeze a chicken by killing it, plucking it, gutting it, and stuffing it with snow.
sentences.zh: 1626年，弗朗西斯·培根正是在庞德广场尝试通过杀死一只鸡、将其拔毛、掏空内脏并塞满雪来深度冷冻它。

sentences.en: So you remember that story, and Bacon gets...
sentences.zh: 所以你还记得那个故事，培根他……

sentences.en: he gets a chill and ends up dying.
sentences.zh: 他着凉了，最后丢了性命。

sentences.en: And so people always remember Bacon, but they don't remember the chicken.
sentences.zh: 因此人们总是记得培根，却不记得那只鸡。

sentences.en: It's the chicken haunt the area.
sentences.zh: 是那只鸡在那个地区阴魂不散。

sentences.en: Well, nothing was seen or heard of it until the Second World War, when firefighters reported seeing a large bird unable to fly because its feathers had been plucked,
sentences.zh: 好吧，直到二战期间才有人看到或听到关于它的消息，当时消防员报告说看到一只大鸟，因为羽毛被拔光而无法飞翔，

sentences.en: running round in circles and pathetically flapping the stumps of its wings.
sentences.zh: 在原地团团转，可怜地拍打着翅膀的残端。

sentences.en: It is still occasionally seen dropping out of the sky with a squawk.
sentences.zh: 人们偶尔还是会看到它伴随着一声尖叫从空中坠落。

sentences.en: It is always...
sentences.zh: 它总是……

sentences.en: That's a good story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好故事。

sentences.en: It is always shivering.
sentences.zh: 它总是在发抖。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So I don't think we're qualified to pronounce on the supernatural.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们没有资格对超自然现象发表高见。

sentences.en: I mean, we're barely qualified to pronounce on the natural.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们对自然现象都勉强算是有资格。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 这倒也是。

sentences.en: So I think...
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得……

sentences.en: Do you have a guest for us today?
sentences.zh: 你今天给我们请来嘉宾了吗？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I have the best guest we could possibly have.
sentences.zh: 而且我请到了我们所能请到的最棒的嘉宾。

sentences.en: It's Roger Clark, who wrote what I think is the best book on ghosts that I've ever read.
sentences.zh: 他是罗杰·克拉克，他写了我认为是我读过的关于幽灵最好的书。

sentences.en: And it's a book, not just about ghosts, but about the history of ghosts.
sentences.zh: 这本书不仅关于幽灵，还关于幽灵的历史。

sentences.en: So absolutely perfect.
sentences.zh: 简直完美。

sentences.en: Ghosts, a natural history, 500 years of searching for proof.
sentences.zh: 《幽灵：自然史，寻证五百年》。

sentences.en: And I read it this Christmas, because obviously at Christmas, you should read a ghoSt...
sentences.zh: 我在这个圣诞节读了它，因为显然在圣诞节，你应该读一个幽……

sentences.en: A book?
sentences.zh: 一本书？

sentences.en: Yeah, ghost stories and things.
sentences.zh: 对，鬼故事之类的内容。

sentences.en: And my wife had bought a kind of chair you get in a gentleman's club.
sentences.zh: 我妻子买了一种你在绅士俱乐部里才能见到的那种椅子。

sentences.en: She bought it on eBay or something.
sentences.zh: 她是在eBay还是什么地方买的。

sentences.en: I put it in front of the fire, glass of sherry, Roger's book.
sentences.zh: 我把它放在壁炉前，一杯雪莉酒，罗杰的书。

sentences.en: One of the great, great reading experiences of my life.
sentences.zh: 这是我一生中最棒的阅读体验之一。

sentences.en: And we'd begun the podcast then.
sentences.zh: 那时我们已经开始了播客节目。

sentences.en: And I thought, we have to get him on.
sentences.zh: 我想，我们一定要把他请来。

sentences.en: And we have to talk ghosts.
sentences.zh: 我们必须聊聊幽灵。

sentences.en: So Roger, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 罗杰，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Such a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 不胜荣幸。

sentences.en: And yes, every day at five o'clock, I was sort of wrapped to see which peculiar story you would pick out.
sentences.zh: 是的，每天五点钟，我都非常着迷地想看看你们会挑出什么奇特的故事。

sentences.en: And yes, I do throw in a few strange ones.
sentences.zh: 没错，我确实加了一些奇怪的故事进去。

sentences.en: Well, there are so many peculiar stories, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 有很多奇特的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because essentially, you are...
sentences.zh: 因为本质上，你正在……

sentences.en: Let's actually begin with a question, which has been sent in by Rob Long.
sentences.zh: 让我们从罗布·朗发来的一个问题开始吧。

sentences.en: And he says, how much does background matter?
sentences.zh: 他问，背景有多大关系？

sentences.en: Are British ghost sightings different, say, to French?
sentences.zh: 英国人看到的鬼魂和法国人看到的有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: How much do the events of the time seem to affect what people report?
sentences.zh: 当时发生的事件在多大程度上影响了人们的报告？

sentences.en: And that essentially is your thesis, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是你的论点，对吧？

sentences.en: That ghost stories evolve to reflect the assumptions and the beliefs and perhaps the tensions and the paranoias of the age in which these ghosts appear.
sentences.zh: 鬼故事的发展反映了这些鬼魂出现那个时代的假设、信仰，以及可能存在的紧张局势和偏执。

sentences.en: Yes, and I didn't really realise this until I started writing the book.
sentences.zh: 是的，在开始写这本书之前我并没有真正意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And I had this sort of childhood obsession with ghosts, and I wanted to see a ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 我对幽灵有一种童年时期的痴迷，我想见一个幽……

sentences.en: And then as I went to university and so forth, I got rather embarrassed by my interest in it
sentences.zh: 然后当我上大学等等之后，我对它的兴趣感到有点尴尬，

sentences.en: and pitched the book.
sentences.zh: 并提出了这本书的构想。

sentences.en: It got written.
sentences.zh: 书写出来了。

sentences.en: And I noticed there was a definite shift in what people wanted from ghosts.
sentences.zh: 我注意到人们对幽灵的需求发生了明确的转变。

sentences.en: And not so much do...
sentences.zh: 与其说是……

sentences.en: I found the question, do ghosts exist, not really very interesting.
sentences.zh: 我发现“幽灵是否存在”这个问题其实并不是很有趣。

sentences.en: I wanted to find out what people wanted from ghosts.
sentences.zh: 我想弄清楚人们对幽灵有什么诉求。

sentences.en: And I realised that you could see definite shifts in what the ghost experiences over about every hundred years.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，大约每隔一百年，你就能看到人们对幽灵经历的诉求发生了明确的变化。

sentences.en: And the other thing from my childhood is that in the seventies is that, you know, we were the poor man of Europe.
sentences.zh: 我童年的另一件事是，在七十年代，你知道的，我们是欧洲的穷国。

sentences.en: We were terrible at everything, but we were really good at ghosts.
sentences.zh: 我们做什么都不行，但我们在闹鬼方面真的很在行。

sentences.en: And we were the most haunted country in the world.
sentences.zh: 我们是世界上闹鬼最严重的国家。

sentences.en: And it was just a marvellous and involving thought.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个奇妙且引人入胜的想法。

sentences.en: And so I wanted to go back and look at that.
sentences.zh: 所以我想要回过头去研究一下。

sentences.en: And why were there so many ghost books and famous ghost hunters?
sentences.zh: 为什么在七十年代会有那么多鬼故事书和著名的捉鬼猎人？

sentences.en: In the seventies, I actually wrote them as a schoolboy.
sentences.zh: 我在学生时代其实就写过这些。

sentences.en: And got sort of involved in discussing ghosts and that there were different kinds of ghosts.
sentences.zh: 并且参与讨论幽灵以及幽灵有不同种类的事。

sentences.en: Clearly, I worked out there are about 10 or so varying kinds of ghosts.
sentences.zh: 很显然，我得出结论，大约有10种左右不同的幽灵。

sentences.en: And it all sort of went from there.
sentences.zh: 一切基本上就是从这里开始的。

sentences.en: And I noticed that there was some specific issues about Britain and England and the UK.
sentences.zh: 我注意到关于英国、英格兰和联合王国有一些具体的问题。

sentences.en: And it involved the Civil War and to quite a big extent, the suppression of Catholicism,
sentences.zh: 这涉及到内战，在很大程度上还涉及到对天主教的镇压，

sentences.en: the comeback of Catholicism in the 1780s and so forth, and this fear of resurgent Catholicism.
sentences.zh: 1780年代天主教的卷土重来等等，以及对天主教死灰复燃的这种恐惧。

sentences.en: But also, you know, the sprinklings of German belief, which came in with the various members of the royal family, obviously all the Celtic stuff.
sentences.zh: 但同时，你知道的，还有随着王室成员到来而传入的德国信仰的点滴，显然还有所有的凯尔特元素。

sentences.en: And it's a very specific mix of belief.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常独特的信仰融合。

sentences.en: And also, we seem to have this specific idea of the sort of comfort that ghost stories are sort of comforting, which is quite, you know, relatively unusual in world culture.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们似乎还有这样一种独特的观念，即鬼故事在某种程度上是抚慰人心的，这在世界文化中可以说是相对罕见的。

sentences.en: You know, why would we want to have this alarming subject as a sort of comforting midwinter thing in particular?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，为什么我们会把这个令人担忧的主题当作一种特别的仲冬时节的慰藉呢？

sentences.en: And if you were to boil it down, Roger, do you think that – so I found your book fascinating, and particularly the stuff about religion and ghosts, sort of linking the two.
sentences.zh: 罗杰，如果你把它归纳一下的话，你认为——我觉得你的书非常引人入胜，尤其是关于宗教和幽灵的那部分，将两者联系在了一起。

sentences.en: I mean, you have a line in your book about belief in ghosts as a sort of decayed form of religion in a secular age or something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在书中有一句话，大意是在世俗时代，对幽灵的信仰是宗教的一种衰退形式之类的话。

sentences.en: But you talk a lot about the influence of the Reformation, so breaking with the Catholic Church and then the Civil War and so on.
sentences.zh: 但你大量讨论了宗教改革的影响，也就是与天主教会的决裂，然后是内战等等。

sentences.en: And do you think it's because of the Reformation that England specifically has this tradition of ghost stories
sentences.zh: 你认为正是因为宗教改革，英格兰才具体拥有了这种鬼故事传统，

sentences.en: and so many kind of monks and nuns and sort of haunted Jesuitical figures and stuff like that?
sentences.zh: 以及那么多僧侣、修女和充满耶稣会色彩的闹鬼人物之类的东西吗？

sentences.en: Yes, the walled-up monks and so forth, they're all essentially regency, what I call off-the-shelf ghosts.
sentences.zh: 是的，那些被封在墙里的僧侣等等，它们本质上都是摄政时期的产物，我称之为现成的鬼魂。

sentences.en: And it's the same with headless carriages and headless horsemen and that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 无头马车和无头骑士之类的情况也是如此。

sentences.en: And again, with acephaly, the headlessness, you can go – it goes almost straight back to, you know, the saints, the – what do you call them?
sentences.zh: 同样，关于无头现象，你可以追溯到——它几乎直接追溯到，你知道的，圣徒，那些——你管他们叫什么？

sentences.en: The cephalophores, the headless saints, which is a long tradition, as you both know.
sentences.zh: 捧头圣徒，无头圣徒，这是一个悠久的传统，正如你们俩都知道的。

sentences.en: So – and I was very interested as to, you know, an Anne Boleyn being quite a – I mean, she's seen in popular culture as a sort of a bit of a sort of dizzy creature.
sentences.zh: 所以——我很感兴趣，你知道的，安妮·博林相当一个——我的意思是，她在流行文化中被视为有点晕乎乎的角色。

sentences.en: But as far as I understand, she was quite a fearsome Protestant believer.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，她是一位相当可怕的新教信徒。

sentences.en: And the idea that she would come back on an anniversary, a bit like a saint, she was almost like a saint's day, these anniversaries, with her head.
sentences.zh: 而且她会在某个周年纪念日回来的这种想法，有点像圣徒，她几乎就像一个圣徒日，这些纪念日，带着她的头颅归来。

sentences.en: And where was she coming from?
sentences.zh: 她是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Was she coming from purgatory?
sentences.zh: 她是从炼狱来的吗？

sentences.en: Which is – and if she was, that means that her whole belief system, if she was coming from purgatory, was incorrect.
sentences.zh: 也就是——如果是这样，那就意味着她的整个信仰体系，如果她是来自炼狱的话，就是不正确的。

sentences.en: And for – there was a while where to believe in ghosts marked you out as a Catholic, which was a dangerous business.
sentences.zh: 而且在有一段时间里，相信幽灵会将你标榜为天主教徒，这是一件危险的事情。

sentences.en: Well, so, Roger, I mean, obviously there's an echo there of perhaps the most famous ghost in English literature, which is the ghost of Hamlet's father.
sentences.zh: 好吧，罗杰，我的意思是，很明显那里有一种回响，也许是英国文学中最著名的幽灵，也就是哈姆雷特父亲的幽灵。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that sense that Hamlet, who studies at Wittenberg, and therefore presumably is a good Protestant, has as a father a ghost who's in purgatory
sentences.zh: 那种感觉是，在维滕贝格求学、因此推测是一个优秀新教徒的哈姆雷特，其父亲却是一个身处炼狱的幽灵，

sentences.en: and who therefore presumably is Catholic.
sentences.zh: 因而推测他是个天主教徒。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a kind of buried element of the play, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是剧中一种隐藏的元素，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of theories that Shakespeare was a secret Catholic and so forth, which I find quite, you know, slightly convincing.
sentences.zh: 有很多理论认为莎士比亚是个秘密天主教徒等等，我觉得这相当，你知道的，稍微有点说服力。

sentences.en: In the same way that maybe M.R.
sentences.zh: 就像M·R·

sentences.en: James had high church leadings that he wanted to conceal from his father, which is why he didn't become a clergyman.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯可能有着他想对父亲隐瞒的高教会倾向，这就是为什么他没有成为一名牧师。

sentences.en: And it's sort of – and you'll notice that a lot of M.R.
sentences.zh: 这有点像——你会注意到M·R·

sentences.en: James' ghosts are to do with pre-Protestant guardian spirits
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯的许多幽灵都与前新教的守护神有关，

sentences.en: and so forth.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So M.R.
sentences.zh: 所以M·R·

sentences.en: James, for those listeners who don't know, is the sort of the supreme exponent of the classic ghost story, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯，对于那些不知道的听众来说，可以说是经典鬼故事的最高代表，对吧？

sentences.en: He's writing at the sort of – when's he writing?
sentences.zh: 他写作的时期大约是——他是什么时候写作的？

sentences.en: Early 20th century, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想是20世纪初吧。

sentences.en: But his stories are always backward-looking, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但他的故事总是回顾过去的，对吧？

sentences.en: And they have that gothic element, which I get the impression from your book that you think the gothic element
sentences.zh: 它们带有那种哥特式元素，从你的书里我得到的印象是你认为哥特式元素

sentences.en: in ghost stories – well, I'm not going to put words in your mouth and say that you think it's fraudulent,
sentences.zh: 在鬼故事中——好吧，我不会强加观点给你，让你觉得你认为它是虚假的，

sentences.en: but that you think – you talk about things being folkloric, which you generally mean –
sentences.zh: 而是你认为——你谈到事情具有民间传说色彩，你通常指的是——

sentences.en: I don't get the sense that you mean that approvingly, and you think that folkloric elements of a ghost story mean that it's, as it were, true.
sentences.zh: 我并不觉得你是带着赞许的意味在说这话，你认为鬼故事中的民间传说元素意味着，从某种程度上讲它是真的。

sentences.en: But you think that that's kind of – people have brought a lot of baggage to the story, if you like.
sentences.zh: 但你认为那是某种——人们为这个故事带来了很多累赘的观念，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: No, I don't mean folkloric disparagingly at all.
sentences.zh: 不，我绝对不是贬义地指民间传说。

sentences.en: I'm, in some sense, a folkloriSt.

sentences.en: And the science side has sort of reached a kind of cul-de-sac for one reason or the other.
sentences.zh: 由于某种原因，科学这一边已经陷入了一种死胡同。

sentences.en: It was very active for over 100 years.
sentences.zh: 它活跃了100多年。

sentences.en: And I think we're now much more seeing ghost stories and things as constructions of all sorts of complicated social mores.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在更多地将鬼故事之类的内容视为各种复杂社会风俗的建构。

sentences.en: And I also talk in the book about the, you know, the British class aspect of ghosts.
sentences.zh: 我在书中也谈到了幽灵的英国阶级属性。

sentences.en: But going back to the Catholicism thing, I mean, you've got, you know, the birth of, you know,
sentences.zh: 但回到天主教的问题上，我的意思是，你拥有，你知道的，

sentences.zh: 《奥特兰托城堡》和沃波尔的诞生，正值整个《天主教解放法案》等等法案艰难推进的时期。

sentences.en: There were several of them.
sentences.zh: 当时有好几个这样的法案。

sentences.en: And you can see this and this, you know, the Gordon riots and this genuine alarm that Catholicism was like crawling back out of the ground, you know,
sentences.zh: 你可以看到这一点，你知道的，戈登暴动以及这种真正的惊恐，即天主教就像是从地下重新爬出来一样，你知道的，

sentences.en: and would bring ghosts with it.
sentences.zh: 并且会把幽灵也一同带回来。

sentences.en: And, you know, you get, that's why you get these sort of spectral and satanic monks in Gothic literature.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是为什么你在哥特文学中会看到这些幽灵般的、撒旦般的僧侣。

sentences.en: M.R.
sentences.zh: M·R·

sentences.zh: 他认为那有点倒胃口。

sentences.en: And he, what's interesting about M.R.
sentences.zh: 而他，M.R.

sentences.zh: 詹姆斯有趣的地方在于，他向来被推崇为我们最伟大的鬼故事作家，即虚构的鬼故事。

sentences.en: And yet what he does is not actually traditional ghosts at all.
sentences.zh: 然而他的所作所为实际上根本不是传统的鬼魂。

sentences.en: They're either these sort of dead, alive, medieval type walking dead, who's a definite thing, the animated corpse.
sentences.zh: 它们要么是那种半死不活的中世纪行尸走肉，也就是确切存在的复活尸体。

sentences.en: Or, as I say, these kind of guardian spirits as a result of sort of versions of black magic and occult practice.
sentences.zh: 或者，正如我所说，是某种黑魔法和神秘实践演变而来的守护精灵。

sentences.en: And so they're really not at all, you know, lonely spirits and things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以它们真的完全不是，你知道的，孤独的灵魂之类的事物。

sentences.zh: 它们相当、相当可怕，而且极其非人、令人不快。

sentences.en: So before we start to look at in more detail at the way that the British understanding of ghosts has evolved from the Reformation and onwards,
sentences.zh: 所以在我们开始更详细地探讨英国人对鬼魂的理解如何从宗教改革及以后演变之前，

sentences.en: can we just broaden the camera back out again?
sentences.zh: 我们能把镜头再拉远一点吗？

sentences.zh: 因为你提到了中世纪的鬼魂。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: That they are kind of subtly different to the ones that we now know.
sentences.zh: 它们与我们现在所知的那些有着微妙的不同。

sentences.en: And then, of course, before that, there's the example of the classical ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，在此之前，还有古典鬼魂的例子。

sentences.en: And from, you know, the story that Dominic narrated at the head of the show, you've got clanking chains.
sentences.zh: 而且从，你知道的，多米尼克在节目开头讲述的故事来看，你有哗啦作响的铁链。

sentences.zh: 你有人需要被埋葬。

sentences.en: So there are clearly elements there that do feed into the kind of the mainstream.
sentences.zh: 所以那里显然有一些元素融入了主流。

sentences.en: And also the Greeks and the Romans thought that ghosts vanished on cock crows and that they appear at midnight and at midday and kind of various elements like that.
sentences.zh: 而且希腊人和罗马人也认为鬼魂在雄鸡啼叫时会消失，它们在午夜和正午出现，还有诸如此类的各种元素。

sentences.en: So how different are, say, classical ghosts to the ghosts that we recognise today?
sentences.zh: 那么，比方说，古典鬼魂与我们今天所认知的鬼魂有多大不同？

sentences.en: And to what extent do those classical stories have an influence on the ghost story as we know it?
sentences.zh: 这些古典故事在多大程度上对我们所知的鬼故事产生了影响？

sentences.en: If you go all the way back to this, you know, Sumerian dead and things, what ghosts were, were, again, sort of half demonic.
sentences.zh: 如果你一直追溯到这个，你知道的，苏美尔人的死者之类的事物，鬼魂是什么，它们同样也是半魔鬼式的。

sentences.en: They weren't really quite people and they weren't really quite ghosts as we understand it.
sentences.zh: 它们其实不太算是人，也不太算是我们所理解的鬼魂。

sentences.en: And this idea of the hungry dead or the dead being unhappy about the way that they'd been buried, which is what you get in the Greek story you mentioned earlier,
sentences.zh: 这种饥饿亡灵的概念，或者死者对他们被埋葬的方式感到不满——也就是你之前在希腊故事中听到的那样，

sentences.en: But as soon as ghosts are seen as sort of people, a bit like you and I, that didn't really happen until, totally until the 1950s where ghosts were just seen as people.
sentences.zh: 但一旦鬼魂被看作某种人，有点像你和我，这种情况直到完全进入20世纪50年代才真正发生，当时鬼魂只是被看作普通人。

sentences.en: You know, you get this gradual procession of very, this archaic idea of the troubled dead, the unburied dead who wanted proper observance made, proper burial made.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你会看到这种渐进的转变：古代那种充满麻烦的死者、未被埋葬的死者，他们希望得到适当的仪式、适当的安葬。

sentences.en: And then in medieval times, you've got the dead who were really just being prepared for the afterlife and were coming back to warn people to live better lives and to be, well,
sentences.zh: 然后在中古时期，你会遇到那些实际上只是在为来世做准备的死者，他们回来警告人们过更好的生活，去……

sentences.en: just to lead better lives, really.
sentences.zh: 真的，只是为了过上更好的生活。

sentences.en: And they were often warnings of their imminent death and they need to get their act together, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 它们往往是对他们即将死亡的警告，他们需要振作起来，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Because my sense of, say, Roman ghosts, and for starters, they don't really have a word equivalent to our ghosts.
sentences.zh: 因为我对，比方说，罗马鬼魂的理解是，首先，它们真的没有一个与我们的“鬼”相对应的词。

sentences.en: I mean, they have kind of various different qualities of shade that might appear.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们有各种不同特质的幽灵可能会出现。

sentences.en: Some are ancestral ghosts, some are more malign.
sentences.zh: 有些是祖先的鬼魂，有些则更加恶毒。

sentences.en: And then the kind of very weird one.
sentences.zh: 然后就是那种非常诡异的。

sentences.en: So the weird one I remember is Brutus, the murderer of Caesar, on the eve of the Battle of Philippi, in which he will end up committing suicide.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得的那个诡异人物是布鲁图斯，凯撒的刺客，在腓力比战役前夕——他最终将在那里自杀。

sentences.en: Kind of seeing, seeing himself and said, you know, I am your, what is it?
sentences.zh: 他似乎看到了，看到了自己并说，你知道的，我是你的，什么来着？

sentences.en: I kind of, I am your fate.
sentences.zh: 我某种程度上说，我是你的命运。

sentences.en: I have come to warn you.
sentences.zh: 我是来警告你的。

sentences.en: And it's kind of a ghost, but it's not quite, is it?
sentences.zh: 这有点像个鬼魂，但又不太像，对吧？

sentences.en: And I suppose you have the sense that we're dealing with things that kind of look familiar, but are strange in ways that we can't quite put our fingers on.
sentences.zh: 我想你会觉得，我们面对的事物看起来似曾相识，却又在某些我们无法确切说出的方面显得十分陌生。

sentences.en: Well, that story is quite interesting because one of the great revelations of the Society for Cycle Research, which was this incredibly august body created in 1882,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个故事相当有趣，因为“灵异研究学会”的重大发现之一——这是一个成立于1882年、极其威严的机构，

sentences.en: full of prime ministers and poet laureates and, you know, extremely eminent scientists, some of whom went on to win Nobel Prizes.
sentences.zh: 里面满是首相、桂冠诗人和，你知道的，极为卓越的科学家，其中一些人后来还赢得了诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: And one of the first things they discovered is called Phantasms of the Living.
sentences.zh: 他们最早发现的事情之一被称为《生者幻象》。

sentences.en: The most common ghosts were ghosts of living people or, you know, and that people were still alive.
sentences.zh: 最常见的鬼魂是活人的鬼魂，或者，你知道的，当时人们实际上还活着。

sentences.en: And this really threw the cat among the pigeons as the idea of what ghosts could possibly be.
sentences.zh: 这确实在鸽群中激起了波澜，颠覆了关于鬼魂究竟是什么的观念。

sentences.en: Surely if they were still alive, then they weren't ghosts in the classical sense.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果他们还活着，那他们在传统意义上就不是鬼魂。

sentences.en: There was some kind of other emanation possibly to do with the science as yet unknown,
sentences.zh: 这可能是某种其他的辐射，可能与尚未为人所知的科学有关，

sentences.zh: 这就是整个科学轨迹的起点，并在相对近期的时候以某种方式结束了。

sentences.en: I guess looking for ghosts that can be explained scientifically, I mean, that is as much a reflection of our age as, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想寻找能够用科学解释的鬼魂，我的意思是，这在很大程度上反映了我们的时代，就像，你知道的，

sentences.en: a Catholic ghost in Protestant England or a Sumerian ghost in Sumeria.
sentences.zh: 信奉天主教的英国之于天主教鬼魂，或是苏美尔之于苏美尔鬼魂一样。

sentences.en: Also, I mean, battle ghosts and battlefields are famous sites, you know, because it's like the Battle of Edge Hill and so forth.
sentences.zh: 还有，我的意思是，战役中的鬼魂和战场是著名的地点，你知道的，因为就像埃奇希尔战役等等。

sentences.en: It was seen in the night sky, you know, afterwards and so forth.
sentences.zh: 人们在夜空中看到了它，你知道的，事后等等。

sentences.en: And this idea of prophecy and, you know, kingship and great men is all part of that romantic mix of power, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这种关于预言、王权和伟人的概念，都是权力的那种浪漫交织的一部分。

sentences.en: I've got a question from one of the listeners asked, just picking up on Tom's point about classical ghosts.

sentences.zh: 我觉得现在是个好时机。

sentences.zh: 这也给汤姆一个机会来谈谈他最喜欢的主题。

sentences.en: So it's about the New Testament where Jesus says he comes back and he says, I'm not a ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这是关于新约的，耶稣说他回来了，他说：“我不是鬼魂。”

sentences.zh: 只是一个普通的那种犹太鬼魂。

sentences.zh: 但是是的，我的意思是，我想你这就切入了三位一体和圣灵的整个问题以及它是如何契合的，这，你知道的，

sentences.zh: 一直是其他宗教嘲笑的对象，你知道的，究竟什么是圣灵，诸如此类。

sentences.zh: 而且你只需拥有这个，你知道的，在古典世界里，你只需拥有令人难以置信的各种幽灵，包含所有你能想象到的种类。

sentences.en: And so it's really, really important, I think, for the writers of the gospel to insist that he, you know, the risen Christ is not one of these various spectres.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为对于福音书的作者来说，坚持认为他——复活的基督不是这些形形色色的幽灵中的一个，真的是非常非常重要。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有趣的是，显然，那里显然有致命的损伤，然而他却某种程度上支撑了下来。

sentences.zh: 基本上，你知道的，“胜利号”战舰就是他的船，诸如此类。

sentences.en: He was the famous man who put down the spithead mutiny and so forth.
sentences.zh: 他是那个平息斯皮特黑德海军兵变等事件的著名人物。

sentences.en: He was absolutely the essence of no nonsense, you know, naval authority.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是绝不胡闹、务实的海军权威的化身。

sentences.en: And he was juSt...
sentences.zh: 他当时正……

sentences.en: And to the end of his days, apparently, he flew into a rage whenever the ghost was mentioned, because he experienced it firsthand and could not explain it, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且据说直到他生命的尽头，每当提到这个鬼魂，他都会大发雷霆，因为他曾亲身经历过且无法解释，你知道的。

sentences.en: So give us the story.
sentences.zh: 所以给我们讲讲这个故事吧。

sentences.en: Give us some of the story for those listeners who don't know it.
sentences.zh: 为那些不知道这个故事的听众讲讲其中的一部分。

sentences.en: So in the sort of 1760s, this woman called Mary Ricketts rented a house with her children in Hampshire and went there.
sentences.zh: 所以在1760年代左右，一个叫玛丽·里科特的女人带着她的孩子在汉普顿租了一栋房子并搬了进去。

sentences.en: And her husband was sort of away in business in the West Indies, so she was very much on her own.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫在西印度群岛做生意不在家，所以她基本上孤身一人。

sentences.en: She took her own servants down there.
sentences.zh: 她把自己的仆人带到了那里。

sentences.en: It was a pretty old, decayed house.
sentences.zh: 那是一栋相当古老、破败的房子。

sentences.en: And pretty soon, a nuisance started, which was lots of banging doors.
sentences.zh: 很快，麻烦就开始了，那就是大量的砰砰关门声。

sentences.en: And it seemed like people were coming in and out of the house and nobody could work on what was going on.
sentences.zh: 看起来好像有人在房子里进进出出，而没有人能弄明白到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: And the London servants all left and there were problems keeping servants.
sentences.zh: 伦敦的仆人们都走了，而且留住仆人也成了问题。

sentences.en: And then they put up a reward notice because they thought, you know, they're offering quite a lot of money, like a year's labourer's wage, rural labouring wage,
sentences.zh: 然后他们贴出了一份悬赏公告，因为他们觉得，你知道的，他们提供相当多的钱，就像一年的农场劳工工资、农村劳动力工资一样，

sentences.en: for information on who was breaking into the house.
sentences.zh: 以换取关于是谁闯入房子的线索。

sentences.en: And it just sort of cascaded on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 这件事就这样没完没了地升级下去。

sentences.en: And these apparitions of a man were seen around the house and then the sound of a woman rushing through.
sentences.zh: 人们在房子四周看到了男人的幻影，接着还听到了女人快步奔跑的声音。

sentences.en: And what we have is a first-hand, almost diary account from Mary Ricketts, which is lodged in the British Library.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的是一份来自玛丽·里科特的第一手、几乎是日记般的记录，现存放在大英图书馆。

sentences.en: And I've sat there reading this day by day, often day by day, account of trying to deal with what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我曾坐在那里阅读这份日复一日、通常是逐日记录的文稿，记录了她试图应对所发生事情的过程。

sentences.en: It's pretty much on her own and being terrified that her children will eventually see the ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 她基本上是孤身一人，并且极度恐惧她的孩子们最终会看到这个鬼魂。

sentences.en: So it's the opposite of a modern ghost story, where it's the children who see the ghosts and the adults don't.
sentences.zh: 所以这和现代鬼故事恰恰相反，在现代故事中，是孩子们看到鬼魂而成年人看不到。

sentences.en: And here, the adult is trying to shield, you know, the children from the ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，成年人正试图保护孩子们免受鬼魂的侵害。

sentences.en: And she, a bit about Mary Ricketts, you know,
sentences.zh: 而她，关于玛丽·里科特，你知道的，

sentences.en: she was extremely well-educated woman with a powerful intellect who was very highly thought of by a lot of members of the clergy who kind of came to her aid.
sentences.zh: 她是一个受过极好教育、智力超群的女性，受到了许多前来施以援手的神职人员的高度评价。

sentences.en: And eventually they had to leave the house.
sentences.zh: 最终他们不得不离开这栋房子。

sentences.en: They couldn't live in it and they went back after.
sentences.zh: 他们无法住在里面，并在之后回去了……

sentences.en: I don't know, well, there were all sorts of awful experiences.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，总之有各种各样的可怕经历。

sentences.en: And midday ghosts, ghosts in the middle of the day and the door being banged.
sentences.zh: 白天的鬼魂、大白天出现的鬼魂以及被猛撞的门。

sentences.en: And I mean, you read about it and you see her handwriting deteriorate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你读到这些时，会看到她的字迹逐渐变糟。

sentences.en: It's really quite striking.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常引人注目。

sentences.en: And she eventually fled to the Bishop's Palace in Winchester, where she was given sanctuary by some of her clerical friends.
sentences.zh: 她最终逃到了温彻斯特的主教府，在那里她得到了几位神职人员朋友的庇护。

sentences.en: And that's how I think the story got eventually relayed to Bishop Benson, the Archbishop of Canterbury, who then told it to Henry James, who turned it into, in my view,
sentences.zh: 我想这就是这个故事最终如何传给坎特伯雷大主教本森主教的经过，然后他将它讲给亨利·詹姆斯听，在我看来，

sentences.en: it's the source story for Turn of the Screw.
sentences.zh: 它是《螺丝在拧紧》的原型故事。

sentences.en: And I just actually found out something recently that M.R.
sentences.zh: 而我最近刚好发现了一些事情，M.R.

sentences.en: James, as an undergraduate, actually went to stay with Bishop Benson in the sort of 1880s and spent Christmas with the same Bishop Benson,
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯在作为本科生时，确实在1880年代左右去拜访过本森主教并与他同住，和同一位本森主教一起度过了圣诞节，

sentences.en: who was then Bishop before he became Archbishop of Canterbury.
sentences.zh: 当时他还是主教，后来才成为坎特伯雷大主教。

sentences.en: And I have this sort of lovely idea that maybe M.R.
sentences.zh: 我脑海里萌生了一个可爱的想法，也许M.R.

sentences.en: James was told this story and maybe he got first dibs on the story and turned it down.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯听过这个故事，并且可能抢先得到了这个故事的版权却拒绝了它。

sentences.en: It's amazing that two of them, yeah, two people called James.
sentences.zh: 真神奇，他们俩，对，两个都叫詹姆斯的人。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: And I can't help thinking that elements of his ghost story called Lost Hearts may have sort of some buried elements of Turn of the Screw.
sentences.zh: 而且我不禁觉得，他那篇名为《失落的心》的鬼故事里，某种程度上也夹杂着一些《螺丝在拧紧》的影子。

sentences.en: But I really wanted to crack the mystery.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很想破解这个谜团。

sentences.en: For me, that was a big mystery.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一个巨大的谜团。

sentences.en: What was this story that Bishop Benson told?
sentences.zh: 主教本森讲的到底是什么故事？

sentences.en: And so what was going on?
sentences.zh: 当时到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Because there is the Battle of Cheriton in the English Civil War that is fought basically on the grounds of Hinton Amna.
sentences.zh: 因为在英国内战期间，切里顿战役基本上就是在辛顿·阿姆纳的土地上打响的。

sentences.en: Well, there's this incredible sort of soundscape of this haunting.
sentences.zh: 这里有一种令人难以置信的、与这种闹鬼现象有关的声景。

sentences.en: It's a very, very noisy haunting.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常非常吵闹的闹鬼事件。

sentences.en: And so there was this sort of, I think there was noise of really of the battle, which I think came up almost to the windows and the door of the house.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，当时真的有战役的声音，甚至我觉得那些声音都传到了房子的窗户和门边。

sentences.en: And it was like it was being replayed, really.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像是在被重播一样。

sentences.en: But that wouldn't explain people going, I mean, nothing would explain it.
sentences.zh: 但这也无法解释人们的所作所为，我的意思是，什么都解释不通。

sentences.en: But usually when you have hauntings, there's some, somebody comes up with some story to explain why there are these presences or what's going on.
sentences.zh: 但通常当发生闹鬼事件时，总会有人编出一些故事来解释为什么会有这些超自然现象，或者到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Well, is there any story?
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么相关的故事吗？

sentences.en: Yes, there was various stories about that there'd been an affair between a member of the household and a senior servant.
sentences.zh: 是的，有各种各样的传言，说是一个家庭成员和一个高级仆人之间有过一段私情。

sentences.en: And again, turn on the screw sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 这又有点像《螺丝在拧紧》那种调调。

sentences.en: And that it was probably, they were probably the apparitions seen.
sentences.zh: 而且人们看到的幽灵很可能就是他们俩。

sentences.en: But I think this is what you'd call a sort of a multiple haunting, that there are a lot of different ghosts doing different things.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这就是所谓的“多重闹鬼”，也就是有很多不同的鬼魂在做不同的事。

sentences.en: Because it's unusual that there's, it's not quite a poltergeist story, is it?
sentences.zh: 因为这种情况挺罕见的，它不太算是一个闹鬼恶作剧的故事，对吧？

sentences.en: There's a banging, but there's not stuff being thrown.
sentences.zh: 会有砰砰的撞击声，但没有什么东西被扔来扔去。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说的对吗？

sentences.en: And the children, who are often, as you say, almost always in the classical kind of, well, what we think of as the kind of classic ghost story,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，在经典的鬼故事中，孩子们几乎总是常常出现的那种人，也就是我们所认为的经典鬼故事那种类型，

sentences.en: the children can see the ghost or they're possessed or they're somehow involved.
sentences.zh: 孩子们能看到鬼，或者他们被附身了，再或者他们以某种方式卷入了其中。

sentences.en: But the children are completely oblivious.
sentences.zh: 但这些孩子却完全一无所知。

sentences.en: Is that what's going on?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And for me, that's such an interesting twiSt.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一个非常有趣的转折。

sentences.en: It's completely opposite of how Hollywood would tell a story.
sentences.zh: 这完全违背了好莱坞讲述故事的方式。

sentences.en: It's actually much more interesting.
sentences.zh: 这其实要有趣得多。

sentences.en: And just this idea of this embattled woman.
sentences.zh: 而且就是这个身处险境的女性的构思。

sentences.en: And I think it's a sort of, it's sort of like a house invasion story.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点像是那种，有点像是一个房屋入侵的故事。

sentences.en: It's like a version of a violent house invasion.
sentences.zh: 这就像是暴力入室抢劫的一个版本。

sentences.en: And I think that's, it's really the sort of, a bit like the Tedworth drama, I suppose, which Tom knows all about, having grown up near there.
sentences.zh: 我想这确实有点像泰德沃斯的那个戏剧，我想汤姆对此非常了解，因为他就是在附近长大的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's another poltergeiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这是另一个恶作剧幽灵。

sentences.en: And the poltergeist, I was intrigued.
sentences.zh: 而且这个恶作剧幽灵让我很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Do I remember this right, that Martin Luther is the first person to use the word poltergeist?
sentences.zh: 我没记错的话，马丁·路德是第一个使用“恶作剧幽灵”（poltergeist）这个词的人吧？

sentences.en: He is supposed to have made the compound word, yes.
sentences.zh: 据说这个复合词是他创造的，是的。

sentences.en: So not only did he cause the reformation, but he came up with poltergeist too.
sentences.zh: 所以他不仅挑起了宗教改革，还想出了“恶作剧幽灵”这个词。

sentences.en: So that's, that's quite a roster of achievement.
sentences.zh: 所以，这算是一份相当了不起的成就清单了。

sentences.en: And then when there is a strange connection between Germany and poltergeist anyway, and so you get before World War II, people saying, well, of course, Nazism,
sentences.zh: 德国和恶作剧幽灵之间本来就有着一种奇怪的联系，所以在二战之前，人们会说，当然啦，纳粹主义、

sentences.en: fascism is there because it's all about noisy, inchoate spiritual forces.
sentences.zh: 法西斯主义之所以存在，是因为它们都与喧嚣、未成型的精神力量有关。

sentences.en: And of course it would come from Germany because it's like poltergeist central.
sentences.zh: 而且它当然会来自德国，因为这里就像是恶作剧幽灵的总部。

sentences.en: Poltergeists in a way seem that the strangest stories to explain, but also the ones perhaps because of that, that hold a mirror up most intriguingly to kind of religious currents.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上看，恶作剧幽灵似乎是最难以解释的故事，但也正因如此，它们或许最引人入胜地为某种宗教思潮照出了一面镜子。

sentences.en: And you see that in the 17th century ghost stories, poltergeist stories like the Tidworth Drummer.
sentences.zh: 你在17世纪的鬼故事中也能看到这一点，比如像泰德沃斯鼓手这样的恶作剧幽灵故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And you see it in this one.
sentences.zh: 你在消灭这个鬼魂的故事中也能看到。

sentences.en: And you also see it in perhaps the most fascinating of all the stories, because it basically, we know that it's a fake, which is the story of the Cochrane ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 你还能在所有故事中最吸引人的一个中看到这一点，因为基本上我们知道这是一场骗局，也就是科克巷幽灵的故事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which features none other than Dr. Johnson.
sentences.zh: 其中的主角正是约翰逊博士。

sentences.en: So can you just tell us a bit about that?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们讲讲那件事吗？

sentences.en: Because that's a great story.
sentences.zh: 因为那是个很棒的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So in the 1760s as well, a chap and his wife had nowhere to stay and they stayed with this family in Cochrane.
sentences.zh: 所以在18世纪60年代左右，有个家伙和他的妻子无处可去，就借住在科克巷的这户人家里。

sentences.en: And then they fell out with the family in Cochrane and the wife died.
sentences.zh: 后来他们跟科克巷的这家人闹翻了，然后妻子就去世了。

sentences.en: And suddenly this news came around that the wife was haunting the house and tapping out a condemnation of her husband, that her husband had murdered her.
sentences.zh: 突然间，有消息传来说妻子的鬼魂在屋里出没，并敲击着指控她丈夫谋杀她的罪行。

sentences.en: Now, the husband was from an educated gentleman class.
sentences.zh: 当时，这个丈夫出身于受过良好教育的绅士阶层。

sentences.en: And the chap whose house he was in, the Parsons family, were just, you know, basically working class people associated with running the nearby church, St. Sepplechers.
sentences.zh: 而他借住房子的主人帕森斯一家，你知道的，基本上是与管理附近教堂（圣塞普尔克雷教堂）有关的工人阶级。

sentences.en: And he then realised that he could charge money.
sentences.zh: 然后他意识到自己可以通过这个赚钱。

sentences.en: And it was all centred around the two little girls and they'd lie in bed and these knocks would come.
sentences.zh: 整件事都围绕着两个小女孩展开，她们躺在床上，就会传来这些敲击声。

sentences.en: And they worked out, you know, certain amounts of raps for yes and one for no.
sentences.zh: 他们琢磨出了一套规则，你知道的，敲几下代表“是”，敲一下代表“不是”。

sentences.en: In fact, I think it was the other way around, unusually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我觉得不同寻常的是，情况正好相反。

sentences.en: Later on, it became one for no.
sentences.zh: 后来才变成敲一下代表“不是”。

sentences.en: And people would come around and suddenly, because there was a rather feverish atmosphere going on, because there was a lot of recently launched newspapers,
sentences.zh: 人们会围拢过来，突然之间，由于当时弥漫着一种狂热的氛围，因为有大量新创办的报纸，

sentences.en: there was a huge expansion in newsprint and newspaper titles.
sentences.zh: 新闻纸和报纸刊物的数量急剧膨胀。

sentences.en: It became a sort of big scandal and people, crowds would gather, hoping to hear the ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 这成了一桩特大丑闻，人们和蜂拥而至的群众都希望能听到鬼魂的声音。

sentences.en: And then members of the royal family would turn up in their coach to hear the ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 然后皇室成员也坐着马车赶来听鬼魂的声音。

sentences.en: And it became a sort of scandal because they had to work out, you know, are we going to treat this as a murder story and what's going on?
sentences.zh: 这演变成了一场丑闻，因为他们必须弄清楚，你知道的，我们是要把它当作谋杀案来处理，还是到底怎么回事？

sentences.en: And so it was sort of investigated and Dr. Johnson was on one of the teams investigating it.
sentences.zh: 所以这件事受到了一定程度的调查，约翰逊博士就是调查团队的成员之一。

sentences.en: And pretty soon the whole thing fell apart, that the father was a drunken.
sentences.zh: 很快整件事就露馅了，原来那个父亲是个酒鬼。

sentences.en: It was basically a sort of pub joke that went wrong.
sentences.zh: 这基本上算是一个搞砸了的酒馆笑话。

sentences.en: But the way that everyone thought that they knew, it was a complete conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 但每个人都觉得自己知情的那种样子，完全就是一个阴谋论。

sentences.en: Everyone thought they knew what was really going on.
sentences.zh: 每个人都自以为知道到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: There was a very sort of feverish feeling.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种非常狂热的情绪。

sentences.en: It was a lot of drunkenness.
sentences.zh: 有很多酗酒现象。

sentences.en: This is really a ghost story about the effect of drink.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一个关于酒精影响的鬼故事。

sentences.en: It's about gin, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是关于金酒的，对吧？

sentences.en: They're all drinking gin.
sentences.zh: 他们都在喝金酒。

sentences.en: They're all absolutely bladded on gin.
sentences.zh: 他们喝金酒喝得酩酊大醉。

sentences.en: And in fact, I discovered subsequent to writing this book, there was also another scandal.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我在这本书写完之后发现，当时还有另一桩丑闻。

sentences.en: It was sort of in the pub another few doors down just a little bit earlier, which was to do with a kind of gay sex scandal.
sentences.zh: 就在几家门面之隔的一家小酒馆里，稍微早一点的时候发生过，跟某种同性恋性丑闻有关。

sentences.en: And so that had also happened on the same street just really months earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以就在几个月前，同一条街上也发生过这种事。

sentences.en: So everyone was just going crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都快疯了。

sentences.en: The Lord Mayor got involved.
sentences.zh: 伦敦市长也介入了。

sentences.en: There was eventually a court case.
sentences.zh: 最终还闹上了法庭。

sentences.en: It's a shame that it turned out to be a fate because I do love the idea of Dr. Johnson as a kind of agent molder.
sentences.zh: 很遗憾这最终被证明是一场骗局，因为我真的很喜欢把约翰逊博士想象成某种军情五处特工的设定。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Investigating ghosts.
sentences.zh: 去调查鬼魂。

sentences.en: There's a great series of novels in that or a sort of TV series.
sentences.zh: 这其中包含了一系列很棒的小说或某种电视剧题材。

sentences.en: Dr. Johnson, Ghost Hunter.
sentences.zh: 《约翰逊博士：捉鬼敢死队》。

sentences.en: Yes, he'd be waiting to be written.
sentences.zh: 是的，这个题材正等待着被人写出来呢。

sentences.en: Well, there's this fantastic scene where he goes down.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个极其精彩的场景，他走了下去。

sentences.en: I mean, I live in Old Street, not far from Clerkenwell.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我住在老街，离克勒肯韦尔不远。

sentences.en: There's this marvellous scene of him going down the staircase into the crypt of the church there.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常精彩的场景，他顺着楼梯走下去，来到了那里的一座教堂地窖里。

sentences.en: I think it's St. Anne's.
sentences.zh: 我想那是圣安妮教堂。

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定。

sentences.en: And because the ghost has promised to knock on the lid of her coffin in the crypt.
sentences.zh: 因为鬼魂承诺会在地窖里敲击她棺材的盖子。

sentences.en: And they're all there craning to hear.
sentences.zh: 他们都在那里伸长了脖子倾听。

sentences.en: And nothing, nothing happens.
sentences.zh: 结果什么都没有，什么都没发生。

sentences.en: And interestingly, that area is also almost certainly where Swedenborg had his vision.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那个地区几乎可以肯定是史威登堡获得神视的地方。

sentences.en: It's also, it's just around the corner from St. Bartholomew the Great, the parish church that was founded originally as a priory by Raheer, supposedly the jester of Henry I.
sentences.zh: 而且它就在大圣巴托罗缪教堂的拐角处，那座教区教堂最初是由亨利一世的小丑拉黑尔作为修道院建立的。

sentences.en: And apparently some workmen in the 19th century were working on his tomb and one of the workmen stole his sandal.
sentences.zh: 据说19世纪有一些工人在他的墓上干活，其中一个工人偷了他的凉鞋。

sentences.en: And ever since, Raheer appears on the day that his sandal was stolen, demanding it back.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，拉黑尔就会在他凉鞋被偷的那天现身，要求把凉鞋讨回来。

sentences.en: So I throw that out.
sentences.zh: 所以我把这个抛出来。

sentences.en: Tom, I've heard that story in a churchyard in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我是在莫斯科的一个教堂墓地里听到这个故事的。

sentences.en: And it's one of those portable stories.
sentences.zh: 这是一个那种到处流传的“万能故事”。

sentences.en: So Stalin had...
sentences.zh: 所以斯大林有……

sentences.en: I'm glad you've debunked Tom in front of all of our listeners.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你在我们所有的听众面前揭穿了汤姆。

sentences.en: It's great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: Anyway, can we juSt...
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我们能不能……

sentences.en: Talk to Johnson both.
sentences.zh: 谈谈约翰逊的经历。

sentences.en: Can we just unpack that story?
sentences.zh: 我们能剖析一下那个故事吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so...
sentences.zh: 好的，所以……

sentences.en: The Cock Lane story.
sentences.zh: 科克巷的故事。

sentences.en: Because there's a couple of elements of that that come up again and again in your book about ghost stories.
sentences.zh: 因为其中有几个元素在你的鬼故事书中反复出现。

sentences.en: One of them is the media and the way in which ghost stories are literally mediated.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是媒体，以及鬼故事被字面意义上进行媒介化的方式。

sentences.en: And the other is technology.
sentences.zh: 另一个是技术。

sentences.en: Because you talked about the new newspapers.
sentences.zh: 因为你谈到了新报纸。

sentences.en: And you talk a lot in your book about...
sentences.zh: 你在书中花了很多篇幅谈论……

sentences.en: You talk about magic lanterns and about photography and x-rays and the cinema and so on.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了幻灯机、摄影、X光以及电影等等。

sentences.en: All in different ways kind of seen as ghostly and involving...
sentences.zh: 所有这些都以不同的方式被视为具有幽灵般的色彩，并涉及……

sentences.en: And it's almost as though ghost stories...
sentences.zh: 而且几乎就好像鬼故事……

sentences.en: Well, it's obviously ghost stories take on the elements of the society they are about.
sentences.zh: 好吧，很明显鬼故事吸收了它们所处社会的元素。

sentences.en: But there are particular things that come up again and again.
sentences.zh: 但有些特定的元素是一再出现的。

sentences.en: So do you think almost that the cult of the ghost story, if you like, or the phenomenon of the ghost would be impossible without the kind of mass media and all that stuff?
sentences.zh: 所以你是否认为，如果没有这种大众媒体和所有这些东西，鬼故事的崇拜，如果你愿意这么叫的话，或者鬼魂现象几乎是不可能的？

sentences.en: I see it all the time now because I spent 10 years as a film critic.
sentences.zh: 我现在一直都能看到这种情况，因为我当了10年电影评论家。

sentences.en: And so I saw a lot of movies.
sentences.zh: 所以我看了大量的电影。

sentences.en: And you see how a movie like The Exorcist will completely bring back the whole idea of possession, which was virtually dead in America until that film came out.
sentences.zh: 你能看到像《驱魔人》这样的电影是如何彻底唤醒人们对附身的整个概念的，在那个电影问世之前，这个概念在可以说是名存实亡。

sentences.en: And then the Amityville Horror, so-called Amityville Ghost, which sort of created the Enfield Poltergeist and things like that.
sentences.zh: 然后是《鬼哭神嚎》（又名阿米蒂维尔恐怖事件），也就是所谓的阿米蒂维尔幽灵，它催生了恩菲尔德恶作剧幽灵之类的事情。

sentences.en: And it's juSt...
sentences.zh: 而且这简直是……

sentences.en: As soon as the influence of the media and the film and everything is not to be underestimated, it's absolutely universal now.
sentences.zh: 一旦媒体、电影和各种事物的影响力不容小觑，它现在绝对是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: It's quite extraordinary to follow.
sentences.zh: 这追踪起来非常非同寻常。

sentences.en: And then they said the ghosts that people are seeing or believe they're seeing are their reflections.
sentences.zh: 然后他们说人们看到或者相信自己看到的鬼魂其实是他们自身的倒影。

sentences.en: They're almost always reflections of a wider cultural story.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎总是更广泛的文化故事的映射。

sentences.en: Is that fair?
sentences.zh: 这样说公平吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I'm going back to technology.
sentences.zh: 我接着谈谈技术。

sentences.en: In the 1890s, you've got this extraordinary period where you could, in Regent Street, where you could walk into a place and have an X-ray done.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪90年代，你经历了这样一个非凡的时期，在摄政街，你可以走进一个地方做X光检查。

sentences.en: And people would juSt...
sentences.zh: 人们简直……

sentences.en: It blew their minds they could walk in front of a machine.
sentences.zh: 能够走到机器前，让他们大开眼界。

sentences.en: And see their bones moving, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，看到自己的骨头在动。

sentences.en: And at the same time, it was more or less when the Lumiere, the first cinema, was being made.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，差不多正是卢米埃尔第一部电影问世的时候。

sentences.en: And there's this like sort of six months where X-rays, who were not immediately used for medical reasons, but used for a while very horrifically for entertainment purposes,
sentences.zh: 有大约六个月的时间，X光没有立即用于医疗目的，而是一段时间内非常可怕地用于娱乐目的，

sentences.en: there was a sort of brief six months where cinema and X-rays were right rival forms of entertainment.
sentences.zh: 曾有过大约六个月的短暂时期，电影和X光是针锋相对的娱乐形式。

sentences.en: And you can see in sort of Georges Méliès doing a sort of basically skeleton film as a result of the whole X-ray thing.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到乔治·梅里爱由于整个X光事件而制作了一种基本上是骷髅的电影。

sentences.en: And it said, I put it in a footnote in my book, that apparently when they tested Marie Curie, who, by the way, was an investigator, a ghost investigator, in her spare time,
sentences.zh: 而且据说，我在书的脚注中写过，显然当他们对玛丽·居里进行检测时——顺便说一句，她在业余时间是一名调查员，一名幽灵调查员——

sentences.en: they found evidence that her cancer and so forth was caused by X-rays and not by the radium and so forth she worked on.
sentences.zh: 他们发现证据表明她的癌症等病症是由X射线引起的，而不是由她研究的镭等物质引起的。

sentences.en: And so, yes, so that was how dangerous it was.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这就是它的危险性所在。

sentences.en: But of course, also you get photographs, don't you?
sentences.zh: 但当然，你也会看到照片，对吧？

sentences.en: And so the appearance of ghosts on photographs is...
sentences.zh: 所以照片上出现鬼魂是……

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's, again, it's a big cultural thing.
sentences.zh: 而且这同样是一个重大的文化现象。

sentences.en: So quite early on, photography was used as a way to debunk ghosts, actually to debunk ghosts.
sentences.zh: 所以很早以前，摄影就被用来揭穿鬼魂，实际上就是为了揭穿鬼魂。

sentences.en: Look how easy it is to fake photographs, you know.
sentences.zh: 你看伪造照片有多容易，你知道的。

sentences.en: And so there's the famous photograph of York Minster, the facade of York Minster, people moving out.
sentences.zh: 所以有一张著名的约克大教堂的照片，约克大教堂的正面，人们在走动。

sentences.en: And they would be very ghostly.
sentences.zh: 而它们会显得非常像鬼魂。

sentences.en: And indeed, when, again, when the first moving cinema was seen, it was considered to be...
sentences.zh: 事实上，当——同样，当人们第一次看到动态电影时，它被认为是……

sentences.en: People remarked, there's a very famous review in Russia about how ghostly all these people would be dead at one point, but yet they'd still be moving around.
sentences.zh: 人们评论说，俄罗斯有一篇非常著名的评论，谈到所有人最终都会死，但他们却依然在四处走动，这些鬼魂会是怎样的情景。

sentences.en: And the whole idea of radio was so fantastically spooky, these voices coming out of the ether.
sentences.zh: 而且收音机的整个概念是如此奇异诡谲，这些声音从以太中传出来。

sentences.en: And the idea of mental radio as a sort of adjunct was pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 精神无线电的概念作为一种辅助手段很快就出现了。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, that lasted right up until the 60s, the idea of mental radio.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，这种精神无线电的概念一直持续到60年代。

sentences.en: So just to dip back into the 18th century again, before we come back to the third great story,
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们回到第三个伟大故事之前，让我们再次回溯到18世纪，

sentences.en: I tell you one of the things that I found so surprising in your book was about Methodism, because I'd never put Methodism and ghosts together as sort of interlinked phenomena.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你，在你的书中我发现最令人惊讶的事情之一就是关于卫理公会，因为我从来没有把卫理公会和鬼魂联系在一起看作是相互交织的现象。

sentences.en: But John Wesley, am I right, was a great believer in ghosts.
sentences.zh: 但约翰·卫斯理，我没记错的话，是一个坚定的鬼魂信仰者。

sentences.en: And belief in ghosts in the 18th century was a kind of a marker of being a MethodiSt.
sentences.zh: 在18世纪，相信鬼魂是成为卫理公会信徒的一种标志。

sentences.en: Now, have I got that right?
sentences.zh: 现在，我理解得对吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think Boswell, talking of Dr. Johnson, was in Scotland and he mentioned about ghosts and his extremely aristocratic ghost said, I fancy you are a MethodiSt.
sentences.zh: 我想博斯沃思在谈论约翰逊博士时，在苏格兰提到鬼魂，他那位极其贵族的幽灵说，我猜你是个卫理公会信徒。

sentences.en: So you were talking about the class distinctions of ghosts.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才在谈论鬼魂的阶级区别。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So even in the afterlife, the British class system.
sentences.zh: 所以甚至在来世，也有英国的阶级制度。

sentences.en: And of course, the Methodists, and there was a Methodist clergyman involved with the cock lane ghost, and he was very much pushed it forward.
sentences.zh: 当然，卫理公会，而且有一位卫理公会牧师卷入了科克巷幽灵事件，他极力推动了这件事。

sentences.en: And it's a sort of hangover of this sort of Joseph Glanville, 1680s idea that even though ghosts were not God, they were a part of a supernatural process which ended up in God.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是约瑟夫·格兰维尔1680年代那种观念的遗留，即尽管鬼魂不是上帝，但它们是超自然过程的一部分，而这个过程最终通向上帝。

sentences.en: So it was like a very crude domestic example of supernatural and power.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是超自然力量的一个非常粗糙的世俗样本。

sentences.en: And that was quite a powerful idea in the 1680s.
sentences.zh: 在1680年代，这是一个相当有影响力的观点。

sentences.en: It sort of fell out of fashion.
sentences.zh: 它有点过时了。

sentences.en: And then the Methodists almost revived it.
sentences.zh: 然后卫理公会几乎将其复活了。

sentences.en: And they very, very, over the years, they kind of very quietly dropped it and pretended it never happened.
sentences.zh: 而且多年来，他们非常、非常安静地放弃了它，假装它从未发生过。

sentences.en: But their founder, who was, of course, involved in, well, he wasn't directly involved, but his family was involved in a famous poltergeist case again.
sentences.zh: 但他们的创始人，当然，他曾卷入——嗯，他没有直接卷入，但他的家人卷入了一起著名的闹鬼恶作剧事件。

sentences.en: And he really, really thought that ghosts existed.
sentences.zh: 他真的、真的认为鬼魂是存在的。

sentences.en: And so, for example, I think the argument he'd used, well, madam, you may not have seen a murder, but they've still happened, whether you've seen it or not, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，我想他会用的论点是，嗯，夫人，你可能没有见过谋杀案，但无论你见过与否，它们还是发生了，你知道的。

sentences.en: And that was weirdly his equivalence about murder.
sentences.zh: 而这奇怪地成了他对谋杀案的类比。

sentences.en: But after, I mean, after the death of the Wesleys, it was quietly dropped.
sentences.zh: 但在此之后，我是说，在卫斯理兄弟去世后，它就被悄悄放弃了。

sentences.en: But there was a very active belief that because of, you know, the Witch of Endor and things like that,
sentences.zh: 但人们有一种非常活跃的信仰，因为，你知道的，恩多尔的女巫之类的事，

sentences.en: that supernatural things were part of a divine penalty and showed that there was much more going on than the basic everyday life worries.
sentences.zh: 超自然事物是神圣惩罚的一部分，这表明除了日常生活的烦恼之外，还有更多的事情在发生。

sentences.en: Well, Roger, obviously, we're recording this in the dead of night, but a sense that dawn is approaching and the cocks may soon be crowing
sentences.zh: 好吧，罗杰，显然我们是在深夜录制这个节目，但有一种黎明将近、公鸡可能很快就会啼鸣的感觉，

sentences.en: and we will have to melt upon the coming of the sun.
sentences.zh: 随着太阳升起我们将消融。

sentences.en: But before that happens, and on the subject of clergymen, can we just talk about perhaps the most famous ghost story in England
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，且就牧师这个话题而言，我们能不能聊聊英国最著名的鬼故事，

sentences.en: that involves a clergyman, which is The Haunting of Borley Rectory, which in the children's book that I mentioned right at the beginning,
sentences.zh: 一个涉及牧师的故事，也就是博利矩正住宅闹鬼事件，我在一开始提到的那本儿童书中，

sentences.en: which had the picture of Athenodorus and the ghost in Athens,
sentences.zh: 里面有雅典诺多罗斯和雅典幽灵的插图，

sentences.en: had a whole chapter on Borley Rectory with ghostly writing on the walls and white ladies and the rectory going up in flames.
sentences.zh: 有一整章都在讲博利矩正住宅，墙上有幽灵文字、白衣女子，还有矩正住宅陷入火海。

sentences.en: And I thought then that it was an incredibly odd story, but that was before I read your book.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得这是一个极其奇怪的故事，但那是在我读你的书之前。

sentences.en: And I realized it was odd to the power of 20.
sentences.zh: 我意识到这是二十倍的奇怪。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a spectacularly odd story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个极其离奇的故事。

sentences.en: So can you just sketch out what was going on in Borley Rectory, the most haunted house in Britain?
sentences.zh: 所以你能大致讲讲英国最闹鬼的房子博利矩正住宅里发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: It was, so it's this house in North Essex, which was a rectory, and it was built...
sentences.zh: 是这样的，这是埃塞克斯郡北部的一栋房子，曾是一座矩正住宅，它建于……

sentences.en: It's early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 这是20世纪初。

sentences.en: Early 20th century, yeah.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初，对。

sentences.en: So in late Victorian times, Reverend Bull went there and he had a big family and his son took over the living.
sentences.zh: 所以在维多利亚时代晚期，布尔牧师去了那里，他有一个大家庭，他的儿子接替了牧师职位。

sentences.en: And what became, what was originally a rather nice house became slowly and slowly more decrepit.
sentences.zh: 原本相当不错的房子慢慢地变得越来越破旧。

sentences.en: But by the sort of 1920s, they couldn't basically get anyone to live there.
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪20年代左右，他们基本上找不到任何人去那里住。

sentences.en: So you had to be a pretty low rent clergyman to get the living there.
sentences.zh: 所以你得是一个相当低端的牧师才能在那里谋生。

sentences.en: And people went there and the people who went there, and it already had an established, there was a nun that walked through the garden and the Bull sisters.
sentences.zh: 人们去那里，去那里的人——那里已经有一种既定的现象，有一个修女在花园里走动，还有布尔家的几个姐妹。

sentences.en: So there were sort of quite a few unmarried sisters who basically felt that the place was very haunted.
sentences.zh: 所以有相当多的未婚姐妹基本上觉得那个地方闹鬼很厉害。

sentences.en: And then it passed on, the living passed on to another man called Lionel Foster.
sentences.zh: 后来，这个牧师职位传给了另一个人，名叫莱昂内尔·福斯特。

sentences.en: And he had this sort of, there's no other way of saying it, kind of crazy wife.
sentences.zh: 他有这样一种——没别的说法，有点疯狂的妻子。

sentences.en: And there was possibly bigamy going on, and she adopted sons, and children then abandoned them, and then fled, and it was, it was absolutely psychodrama.
sentences.zh: 可能还存在重婚现象，她收养了男孩，然后孩子们抛弃了他们，接着又逃跑了，这简直是一场心理剧。

sentences.en: And Harry Price, the famous investigator, went, basically hired it for six months, and did almost like a closed, a very famous investigation using all, you know,
sentences.zh: 著名的调查员哈里·普赖斯去了那里，基本上租了六个月，做了一次近乎封闭式的、非常著名的调查，使用了所有，你知道的，

sentences.en: absolute TikTok technology of the time.
sentences.zh: 当时绝对最前沿的技术。

sentences.en: And he was this famous ghost hunter who was a sort of very interesting character who was basically a paper bag salesman who wanted to be accepted by all the knobs at the SPR,
sentences.zh: 他是那个著名的捉鬼敢死队成员，是一个非常有趣的人物，基本上是个纸袋销售员，渴望被精神研究协会（SPR）的所有大人物接受，

sentences.en: and they all looked down on him.
sentences.zh: 而他们都瞧不起他。

sentences.en: And so he went from being a sort of professional sceptic to a professional believer, because he realised that you could do better, you're just going to make money.
sentences.zh: 所以他从一个职业怀疑论者变成了一个职业信仰者，因为他意识到你可以做得更好，你只要去赚钱就行了。

sentences.en: There's more money in the belief, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 相信这种事更有赚头，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, so he famously said that people prefer the bunk to the debunk.
sentences.zh: 对，所以他有句名言：比起揭穿迷信，人们更喜欢迷信本身。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, and so he investigated it for a while, and there's a huge amount of interesting stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，他调查了一段时间，里面有大量有趣的内容。

sentences.en: Again, very controversial.
sentences.zh: 同样，非常有争议。

sentences.en: He appeared to study, he appeared to find all sorts of inexplicable events happening, sort of spontaneous fires and things like that.
sentences.zh: 他似乎在研究中发现各种各样的神秘事件发生，比如自燃之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then eventually, sort of come the end of the 30s, the Church of England sort of sold it off, really.
sentences.zh: 然后到了30年代末，英国国教会基本上把它卖掉了。

sentences.en: And it was bought by a black shirt, because who did sort of...
sentences.zh: 它被一个黑衫党买下了，因为他做过那种……

sentences.en: You see, that's the bit I didn't get in my children's casebook.
sentences.zh: 你看，这就是我在儿童案例集中没看懂的那部分。

sentences.en: He used to do black shirt village fates in the garden, and then it sort of caught fire, and there's a wonderful woodprint of it in, again,
sentences.zh: 他过去常在花园里举办黑衫党乡村游园会，后来房子着火了，又有一幅精彩的木刻版画，

sentences.en: one of my children's books, of the rectory on fire.
sentences.zh: 在我的一本儿童书里，画的是着火的矩正住宅。

sentences.en: And you can see all the ghostly figures in the flames.
sentences.zh: 你能看到火焰中所有幽灵般的身影。

sentences.en: It's almost certain that he set it on fire as a kind of insurance thing.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定是他为了骗保放火烧的。

sentences.en: But...
sentences.zh: 但是……

sentences.en: And then the ruins were haunted too, and there was a famous photograph of a floating brick.
sentences.zh: 然后废墟也闹鬼了，有一张著名的照片拍到了一块漂浮的砖头。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那个。

sentences.en: The original photograph shows a floating brick, but that was actually just a cropped version of another photograph in which you can see a builder throwing bricks in the corner.
sentences.zh: 原始照片显示一块砖头悬浮着，但实际上那只是另一张照片的裁剪版本，在原图里你能看到一个建筑工人在角落里扔砖头。

sentences.en: And so...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: Dominic, you and your relentless scepticism.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你有着挥之不去的怀疑精神。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: It costs a lot of money to reproduce that picture, yes, from the Underwood Estate.
sentences.zh: 复制那张照片花了不少钱，是的，从安德伍德庄园买来的。

sentences.en: So, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: But again, it's sort of one of these sort of...
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，这也是那种……

sentences.en: And to this day, you just get dozens of paranormal tourists just going there, camping out, sort of to the great bother often of the locals who don't really necessarily like it.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，你还会看到大批超自然现象游客去那里露营，这往往给当地居民带来了很大的困扰，他们其实并不怎么喜欢这样。

sentences.en: But...
sentences.zh: 但是……

sentences.en: And there was a dramatisation on TV about it.
sentences.zh: 电视上还关于它拍过一部戏剧改编作品。

sentences.en: So, it's sort of...
sentences.zh: 所以，可以说是……

sentences.en: Sometimes in ghost stories, the people are much more interesting than the ghosts, and this is one of those occasions.
sentences.zh: 有时在鬼故事中，人比鬼要有趣得多，这就是其中一个例子。

sentences.en: And, Roger, am I right?
sentences.zh: 罗杰，我没说错吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I know in your book and in other interviews, you've sort of said you don't really like the...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道在你的书和其他采访中，你曾说过你其实并不喜欢……

sentences.en: You don't find it interesting, the conversation about, you know, are ghosts real?
sentences.zh: 你觉得关于“鬼魂是真的吗”这种讨论毫无兴味，

sentences.en: Do you believe in ghosts and stuff?
sentences.zh: 你相信有鬼吗之类的话题？

sentences.en: But are there particular stories in the sort of English ghost tradition that you are drawn back to and you think, there's really something very spooky?
sentences.zh: 但在英国鬼故事传统中，有没有某些特定的故事让你流连忘返，并觉得其中确实有些非常诡异的东西？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: Yeah, for me, the Hinton one.
sentences.zh: 对，对我来说，欣顿的那个故事。

sentences.en: Because that is just so relentless and over such a long time and such good quality witnesses.
sentences.zh: 因为那个故事实在是挥之不去，持续了那么长时间，而且目击者的素质那么高。

sentences.en: And there's always been a problem with witnesses.
sentences.zh: 而且关于目击者一直存在一个问题。

sentences.en: Also, a class issue with witnesses.
sentences.zh: 同样，目击者也存在阶级问题。

sentences.en: So, until really the 1920s, the Society for Cycle Research wouldn't take reports from servants.
sentences.zh: 所以直到20世纪20年代，精神研究协会根本不接受来自仆人的报告。

sentences.en: They just would not run them, you know, because they thought they were probably up to no good anyway.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不予采纳，你知道的，因为他们认为这些人反正可能也不是什么好人。

sentences.en: So, there's this huge issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: And there are quite a lot of incidents where a lot of hauntings were actually problematic.
sentences.zh: 有相当多的事件表明，许多闹鬼事件实际上都存在问题。

sentences.en: So, servants either getting in boyfriends and girlfriends or, you know, or stealing or, you know, or just taking out resentments on their mistress and master.
sentences.zh: 因此，仆人们要么是带了男朋友或女朋友回家，要么是偷窃，或者只是在对他们的女主人和男主人发泄怨恨。

sentences.en: But, yeah, for me, the Hinton one still, it does give me the chills, definitely.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，对我来说，欣顿的那个故事仍然让我不寒而栗，绝对是的。

sentences.en: But I think a lot of the best ghost things are probably not stories.
sentences.zh: 但我认为许多最好的鬼故事可能都不是故事。

sentences.en: They're just little incidents, you know.
sentences.zh: 它们只是小插曲，你知道的。

sentences.en: And, of course, we're in a culture that likes a beginning, middle, and an end.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们身处一个喜欢有头有尾的文化中。

sentences.en: But, actually, most ghost accounts you read are not a story and they never find out who the ghost is or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你读到的大多数鬼故事都不是一个完整的故事，而且人们永远不会知道鬼魂是谁或诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Do you think there's anything –
sentences.zh: 你认为有什么——

sentences.en: are 21st century ghosts emerging?
sentences.zh: 21世纪的鬼魂正在出现吗？

sentences.en: And if so, is there anything distinctive about them, do you think?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，你认为它们有什么独特之处吗？

sentences.en: Yes, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对有。

sentences.en: Well, you're now getting ghost stories about Zoom calls.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你现在能看到关于Zoom通话的鬼故事了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So –
sentences.zh: 所以——

sentences.en: Yeah, ghost in the machine.
sentences.zh: 机器里的幽灵。

sentences.en: Ghost in the machine.
sentences.zh: 机器里的幽灵。

sentences.en: And people getting text messages from dead people, people being buried with their phones and carrying on sending text messages.
sentences.zh: 人们收到死者的短信，人们带着手机下葬并继续发送短信。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good one.
sentences.zh: 对，这个不错。

sentences.en: My favourite one is Haunted Autocorrect.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的是“闹鬼的自动纠错”。

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Instead of doing the obvious word, it would say things like dead, buried in cellar, that sort of –
sentences.zh: 它不会输出显而易见的词，而是会说诸如“死了”、“埋在地窖里”之类的话，那种——

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I find that quite disturbing as somebody who spends every day staring at Word documents.
sentences.zh: 作为一个每天盯着Word文档发呆的人，我发现这相当令人不安。

sentences.en: Well, there's been a film recently, too, about – I think it was a lockdown ghost film and it's just about four people on a Zoom call and it's a ghost story
sentences.zh: 嗯，最近也出了一部电影——我想是一部封城期间的鬼片，讲的就是四个在Zoom通话中的人，这是一个关于

sentences.en: about what happens to those people on a Zoom call.
sentences.zh: Zoom通话中的这些人会遭遇什么的鬼故事。

sentences.en: And it's been – I haven't seen it yet myself, but it's been very well received.
sentences.zh: 这部片子——我自己还没看，但反响非常好。

sentences.en: And a lot of those sort of Japanese horror, like Ring and everything like that, is all about surveillance cameras, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 而且很多那种日本恐怖片，比如《午夜凶铃》之类的一切，都与监控摄像头有关，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: It's very much – we've very much gone back to technology.
sentences.zh: 这非常贴切——我们很大程度上又回到了技术本身。

sentences.en: And one other question that occurs to me.
sentences.zh: 我脑海中浮现的另一个问题。

sentences.en: You talk a lot in the book about national specificity.
sentences.zh: 你在书中多次谈到民族特异性。

sentences.en: So there's a fantastic line you have, which I was dying to quote, from the antiquarian Francis Grose,
sentences.zh: 所以你有一句精彩绝伦的台词，我一直渴望引用，出自古董学者弗朗西斯·格罗斯之口，

sentences.en: 18th century antiquarian.
sentences.zh: 18世纪的古董学者。

sentences.en: And he says, dragging chains is not the fashion of English ghosts, chains and black vestments being chiefly the accoutrements of foreign specters seen in arbitrary governments.
sentences.zh: 他说，拖着沉重的铁链可不是英国鬼魂的时尚，铁链和黑色法衣主要是在专制政府中看到的外国幽灵的装备。

sentences.en: Dead or alive,
sentences.zh: 不论生死，

sentences.en: English spirits are free.
sentences.zh: 英国的精灵都是自由的。

sentences.en: I found that so cheering.
sentences.zh: 我发现这太令人振奋了。

sentences.en: And presumably post-Brexit, do you think English spirits will acquire more sort of national specificity?
sentences.zh: 据推测，在英国脱欧后，你认为英国的精灵会获得更多的民族特异性吗？

sentences.en: Haven't they just dug up a Roman skeleton with manacles?
sentences.zh: 他们不是刚刚才出土了一具戴着手铐的罗马时代骷髅吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they did.
sentences.zh: 对，他们确实找到了。

sentences.en: Yes, in a ditch.
sentences.zh: 是的，在一个沟渠里。

sentences.en: And I saw that there was speculation from some archaeologists or historians that that may have been a way of staying them,
sentences.zh: 我看到一些考古学家或历史学家推测，这可能是一种镇压他们的方式，

sentences.en: keeping them dead.
sentences.zh: 让他们保持死状。

sentences.en: I think that's the most popular theory.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是最受欢迎的理论。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because the theory was initially that it's a slave and it may well have been a slave.
sentences.zh: 因为最初的理论是这是一个奴隶，而且他很可能就是一个奴隶。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the fact that he's been chucked in a grave, you know, with the manacles on, which are quite expensive, suggests that there is some attempt to stop him from roaming.
sentences.zh: 但事实上他被扔进了一个坟墓里，你知道的，还戴着当时相当昂贵的手铐，这表明有人试图阻止他四处游荡。

sentences.en: Well, you sort of, you know, in Venice, and there's a famous burial line in Venice, which was partly excavated and they would find people with stones in their mouths
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，在威尼斯，威尼斯有一个著名的墓葬群，部分被发掘出来，人们发现死者嘴里含着石头

sentences.en: to stop them being vampires and weights being put on the dead.
sentences.zh: 以防止他们变成吸血鬼，并在死者身上压上重物。

sentences.en: And it's literally putting physical impediments
sentences.zh: 这简直就是施加物理阻碍

sentences.en: on the dead.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.en: But yes, I mean, of course, but Dickens, of course, used clanking chains for,
sentences.zh: 但是，对，我的意思是，当然，狄更斯当然用哗啦作响的铁链来形容，

sentences.en: for, you know, Christmas Carol
sentences.zh: 为了，你知道的，《圣诞颂歌》

sentences.en: and made it very good.
sentences.zh: 而且写得非常精彩。

sentences.en: Now, a producer just sent me a text message that says European ghosts are covered in red tape, not chains.
sentences.zh: 现在，有个制片人刚刚给我发了一条短信，说欧洲的鬼魂身上缠的都是繁文缛节，而不是铁链。

sentences.en: That tells you where a producer's coming from.
sentences.zh: 这说明了制片人的立场。

sentences.en: Anyway, Tom, the cock has crowed, has it?
sentences.zh: 言归正传，汤姆，公鸡打鸣了，是吗？

sentences.en: The cock has just crowed, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想公鸡刚刚打鸣了。

sentences.en: Did you just organise that on your computer as a sort of special sound effect?
sentences.zh: 你刚才是不是在电脑上搞了个类似特殊音效的东西？

sentences.en: No, it's because, obviously, the cock outside has woken up.
sentences.zh: 不是，这是因为，很显然，外面那只公鸡醒了。

sentences.en: You've done this especially for Roger.
sentences.zh: 你这是专门为罗杰准备的。

sentences.en: He doesn't normally do this on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 他平时在播客里可不这样。

sentences.en: The sun is coming and I think that we need to get away quickly before we melt and dissolve.
sentences.zh: 太阳出来了，我想我们得赶紧离开，免得我们融化消散。

sentences.en: Oh, there it is again.
sentences.zh: 哦，又来了。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 你看。

sentences.en: Eerie.
sentences.zh: 真诡异。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: You wouldn't believe he's a grown man.
sentences.zh: 你真不敢相信他是个成年人。

sentences.en: Roger, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 罗杰，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: That's been absolutely fantastic.
sentences.zh: 这期节目简直太棒了。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 别客气。

sentences.en: Anyone who wants to know more, do check out his sensational book.
sentences.zh: 任何想了解更多信息的人，一定要去看看他那本轰动的书。

sentences.en: I mean, I saved it up for Christmas, but I think even in the dead of June, it would send a shiver down your spine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我本来打算留到圣诞节看，但我觉得即使在炎热的六月，它也会让你不寒而栗。

sentences.en: Yeah, I read it.
sentences.zh: 对，我读过了。

sentences.en: I read it this weekend in a blazing sunny day.
sentences.zh: 我这个周末在阳光灿烂的日子里读的。

sentences.en: Were you frightened?
sentences.zh: 你害怕了吗？

sentences.en: I don't scare easily, Tom, but I was absolutely fascinated.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我可没那么容易被吓到，但我完全被迷住了。

sentences.en: I was really, I think, it's such an interesting subject.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得，这是一个非常有趣的主题。

sentences.en: And the weird thing is, whether you believe in ghosts or not is completely immaterial, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 诡异的是，不管你信不信鬼，其实都无关紧要，对吧？

sentences.en: Because ghosts are such a great window.
sentences.zh: 因为鬼魂是了解过去的一个绝佳窗口。

sentences.en: They're literally immaterial.
sentences.zh: 它们字面意思上也是虚无缥缈的。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I'm glad you spotted that.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你发现了这个双关。

sentences.en: And on that note, there's such a great window onto the paSt.
sentences.zh: 顺着这个话题，它们真的是了解过去的绝佳窗口。

sentences.en: And on that note, thanks ever so much.
sentences.zh: 借此机会，非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: We will be back next week.
sentences.zh: 我们下周再见。

sentences.en: Thank you to Roger.
sentences.zh: 谢谢罗杰。

sentences.en: Thank you to listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: We will see you soon.
sentences.zh: 我们很快再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》。
